title: Werder Bremen win 3-0 at Ochsenhausen to go third in the Bundesliga as Mühlhausen beat Dortmund
seo_title: Bremen win at Ochsenhausen to go third in TTBL
description: Werder Bremen beat TTF Ochsenhausen 3-0 to take third in the Tischtennis Bundesliga, as Post SV Mühlhausen beat Dortmund 3-2 for a fourth straight win.
standfirst: Kirill Gerassimenko came from 5-2 down in the decider against Ochsenhausen's teenager Tiago Abiodun, and Steffen Mengel and the doubles took Mühlhausen past Wim Verdonschot's two wins.
body: Werder Bremen won 3-0 at TTF Ochsenhausen on Monday night to take third place in the Tischtennis Bundesliga from their hosts, while Post SV Mühlhausen beat Borussia Dortmund 3-2 for a fourth straight win as matchday nine finished.

Bremen, Ochsenhausen and 1. FC Saarbrücken are all on 12 points, six behind the unbeaten leaders Borussia Düsseldorf, with Bremen ahead of Ochsenhausen on game difference. Ochsenhausen won their first six matches of the season and have now lost three in a row.

Ochsenhausen were without Shunsuke Togami, who won WTT Star Contender Muscat on Saturday ([Eleven's finals report](/news/wtt-star-contender-muscat-2026-finals-honoka-hashimoto-shunsuke-togami-titles.html)), and fielded three players aged 20 or younger. Irvin Bertrand gave Bremen the lead, beating the 20-year-old Iulian Chirita, the world No 70, 11-9, 11-6, 5-11, 11-8.

The second singles was the closest match of the night. Tiago Abiodun, 18, took Kirill Gerassimenko, the world No 62, to a deciding game and led it 5-2, but Gerassimenko won nine of the last 10 points to take it 11-6. Mattias Karlsson, back in the side this month after the finger injury that kept him out of the European Championships, then beat Daniel Berzosa 11-8, 4-11, 11-9, 11-2. It was Bremen's third win in a row, after victories over Dortmund and TTC Bergneustadt.
Gerassimenko said: "I'm very pleased. Ochsenhausen weren't at full strength, they played without Togami. Even so, it's a very good result for us." (translated from German)

Ochsenhausen's coach, Bogdan Pugna, said his side had faced "a team with a lot more experience than us". He added: "We're still learning. We lacked a bit of consistency, but overall they were simply better." (translated from German)
## Verdonschot's double not enough for Dortmund

In Mühlhausen, Dortmund played without Anders Lind and Kristian Karlsson. Ovidiu Ionescu, the 37-year-old Romanian, beat João Geraldo, the world No 40, 11-7, 6-11, 11-8, 12-10, before Wim Verdonschot levelled by beating Marcos Freitas in four games.

Steffen Mengel, 38, lost the first game to Adam Szudi and trailed 7-1 in the second, but won it 14-12 and went on to win 3-1. "It was pretty scrappy. I started well, but then completely lost the thread," Mengel said, calling it a hard-fought win. (translated from German)

Verdonschot, 21 and the world No 41, kept Dortmund in the tie by coming from two games down against Ionescu, winning the fourth game 11-1 and the fifth 11-8, and kissed the club badge afterwards. Mühlhausen won the deciding doubles 11-3, 8-11, 11-9, 11-2 against Szudi and Cedric Nuytinck.
Mühlhausen lost their first three matches of the season and are now fifth with 10 points, level with TTC Bad Homburg. Dortmund are seventh on eight.

The league breaks for the Mixed Team World Cup and the WTT Finals. Matchday 10 starts on 11 December, when Grünwettersbach play Bad Homburg; Bremen are at home to TSV Bad Königshofen on 13 December (2pm UK) and Ochsenhausen play Mühlhausen on 15 December (6pm UK). Results and the table are on Eleven's [Bundesliga page](/clubs/bundesliga.html); [Sunday's report](/news/tischtennis-bundesliga-2026-27-matchday-9-ionescu-beats-fan-zhendong-dusseldorf-win.html) covers the rest of the round.
